command_words.Show that: Prove a given result; every step must be shown (answer given).
command_words.Hence: Use the previous result to reach the answer.
command_words.Hence or otherwise: Using the previous result is expected, but any valid method earns the marks.
command_words.Find: Work out; method marks need working.
command_words.Calculate: Work out from given facts; show working.
command_words.Sketch: Draw the shape with key features labelled (intercepts, asymptotes, turning points), not to scale.
command_words.Exact: Give the answer in surd, fraction, pi or ln form, not a decimal.
command_words.Verify: Show that given values satisfy the statement.
command_words.Interpret: Explain the meaning of a result in the context of the question.

kcs.title: Binomial and Poisson distributions
kcs.guidance: Students will be expected to use these distributions to model a real-world situation and to comment critically on their appropriateness. Cumulative probabilities by calculation or by reference to tables. Students will be expected to use the additive property of the Poisson distribution, e.g. if the number of events per minute $\sim \text{Po}(\lambda)$ then the number of events per 5 minutes $\sim \text{Po}(5\lambda)$.

kcs.title: Probability density and distribution functions
kcs.statement: The probability density function and the cumulative distribution function for a continuous random variable.
kcs.raw: The probability density function and the cumulative distribution function for a continuous random variable.
kcs.guidance: Use of the probability density function $f(x)$, where $P(a < X \le b) = \displaystyle\int_a^b f(x)\,dx$. Use of the cumulative distribution function $F(x_0) = P(X \le x_0) = \displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{x_0} f(x)\,dx$. The formulae used in defining $f(x)$ will be restricted to simple polynomials which may be expressed piecewise.
